misconceptions.description: Assuming gecko adhesion is mainly suction based
misconceptions.trigger: learner explains attachment using vacuum or suction cup logic
misconceptions.feedback: Gecko-inspired dry adhesion is primarily explained through contact splitting and van der Waals interactions, not suction.

misconceptions.description: Ignoring the directional nature of the adhesive
misconceptions.trigger: learner assumes grip and release behave the same in every loading direction
misconceptions.feedback: Directional adhesion works because geometry changes the contact response depending on whether the load is shear-dominant, normal, or peeling.

misconceptions.description: Thinking biomimicry means copying visible hairs without modeling contact mechanics
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes a gecko-inspired surface based on appearance alone
misconceptions.feedback: What matters is not only that the structure looks hair-like, but that spacing, angle, compliance, and contact splitting create the intended adhesion behavior.
